basics.name: Shailendra Kumar
basics.label: Head of AI, Pan-United
basics.summary: Head of AI at Pan-United, Singapore. Built the company's AI function from zero and leads an 8-person team shipping generative-AI systems into logistics, finance and procurement.

work.name: Pan-United Corporation
work.position: Head of AI (Data Scientist 2020 → Senior Data Scientist 2021 → Assistant Manager 2022 → Manager, AI and Analytics 2024 → Head of AI)
work.summary: Built the AI function from zero; leads an 8-person team shipping generative-AI and ML systems into logistics, finance and procurement.
highlights: Logistics documents read by a vision model: Delivery orders and weighbridge slips read by a vision LLM and pushed straight into the Go Truck app.
Credit assessment from financial statements: A multi-agent system reads statements, payment history and ratios in parallel and assembles a credit view in minutes.
Quotations turned into purchase requisitions: A vision model extracts line items, prices and terms from supplier PDFs and photos and drafts the requisition.
Accounts payable matched against Oracle ERP: Agents extract and cross-check purchase orders, invoices and delivery notes, with human checkpoints where a wrong match costs money.
Daily order forecasting: An LSTM network forecasts daily order volumes at 86% accuracy and feeds resource and inventory planning.
Signature verification: ResNet-50 with triplet loss verifies signatures on delivery paperwork; F-score 0.88.
Voice analytics and chatbot: Whisper-based analytics on customer calls, plus a context-aware chatbot built on the same foundation.
Order-to-cash and SME default prediction: Random Forest predicts invoice payment timing; logistic regression flags SME default risk, with Tableau dashboards for the credit team.
Real-time GPS data platform: A big-data platform on Google Cloud ingests live GPS from the truck fleet for operational visibility.
Client programmes abroad: Deep-learning operations transformation for BridgeMan in New Zealand; automated financial reporting for Eugene Corporation in South Korea.

work.name: Accenture
highlights: Pearson supply-chain transformation: An automated inventory-optimisation tool deployed in 12+ countries; US$35M inventory and US$5M P&L saved in one year.
Kellogg's Europe demand forecasting: An automated ETL and sales-forecasting pipeline for 1,500+ SKUs across 14 countries; accuracy 62.5% to 75%.
Pratt & Whitney supplier delay prediction: K-Means and Random Forest predict late deliveries of aircraft-engine components at 84% accuracy.
Pearson book returns and adoption: Pipelines over large unstructured datasets; book-return prediction over a 3-month horizon at 80% accuracy.

highlights: Fuel-cell shop-floor data platform: A .NET and SQL Server data-acquisition platform with an ASP.NET front end, deployed on six shop floors; 1,000+ QC hours saved.
